## GET /admin-api/announcements

`getConsoleAnnouncements`

**Announcements the console's receiver took in**

What an open console tab collects (#1086): the announcements this realm's admin-console receiver took in after `since` — the `now` this operation answered the tab's FIRST ask with — and within `ssf.announcementKeepS`, oldest first. With no `since` it answers only `now`, so a tab shows what arrived after it signed in. `everyMs` is how often to ask again.

**Mirrors** `no console page — the announcement banner every console page draws, fed by POST /admin/broadcast (#1086)` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `since` | query | integer |  | The `now` of the first answer, in milliseconds. |

**200**: `now`, `everyMs` and `announcements`.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `announcements` | list |  |  |
| `announcements[].at` | string |  |  |
| `announcements[].id` | string |  |  |
| `announcements[].message` | string |  |  |
| `everyMs` | number |  |  |
| `now` | number |  |  |

## GET /admin-api/broadcast

`getBroadcast`

**What an announcement can reach from this realm**

The applications an announcement can be shown in (`surfaces`: `id` and `label` — the admin console, the user portal and the reports application, this service's own Shared Signals receivers), whether the caller may send to `everyRealm` (a service administrator in the default realm), the longest message (`maxChars`), how often an open tab checks (`pollMs`), and whether anything can be delivered (`ready`, with `why` when not). Sending is POST /admin-api/broadcast/send.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/broadcast` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

## POST /admin-api/broadcast/send

`sendBroadcast`

**Show an announcement to everybody signed in**

Sends this service's own `announcement` Security Event Token on the receiver streams of the chosen applications, and every tab of them open at the time shows `message` in a banner within `ssf.internalPollMs` + `ssf.announcementPollMs`. A tab opened later does not. `everyRealm` sends it in every realm, and is refused (STS-SSF-0153) to anybody but a service administrator in the default realm. Answers how many streams took it per realm; `sent: 0` with `why` (STS-SSF-0154) when none did.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/broadcast` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

## GET /admin-api/signals

`getSignals`

**Every security event delivered TO this console**

This service's own admin console is a registered Shared Signals receiver: it has a stream of its own (`sts-admin-console`), seeded in EVERY trust realm, asking for every CAEP and every RISC event type, and each event is POSTed to it over RFC 8935 push at /admin/signals/receive with that stream's own bearer token. This is what arrived.

**IT IS SEEDED IN EVERY REALM AND THE CONSOLE'S CLIENT ENTRY IS IN ONE**, and the disagreement is deliberate: a client entry is about signing somebody IN, and this console's gate reads the DEFAULT realm's session wherever it is reached; a stream is about what HAPPENED, and events happen in the realm they happen in.

**READ `status.why` BEFORE CONCLUDING NOTHING HAS HAPPENED.** An empty `received` has five causes and only one of them is that: `ssf.enabled` off, `ssf.internalReceivers` off, the stream deleted (it is an ORDINARY stream — delete it here or at /admin/ssf and it stays deleted until a restart), `ssf.pushDelivery` off, or `caep.enabled` / `risc.enabled` off under it.

**WHAT A PERSON SEES IS A DIFFERENT RECEIVER.** The user portal has a stream of its own and shows each person only the events whose subject is them; there is no operation here for that view, because it is a person's own page and not an administrative one.

The inbox is IN MEMORY, per trust realm, capped at `ssf.maxReceivedEvents`. The durable record of every delivery is GET /admin-api/audit, which cannot be cleared.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/signals` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sigq` | query | string |  | Narrows the list to rows whose event name, type URI, subject, issuer, audience, `jti` or stream id contains this. One box over all of them, because a reader arrives holding one and does not know which column it is in. |
| `receivedPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the delivered events. Clamped, like every page parameter here. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |

**200**: This receiver and its stream, and the delivered events.

## POST /admin-api/signals/clear

`clearSignalsInbox`

**Empty the console's Shared Signals inbox**

Drops every delivered event held for the admin console in this trust realm.

**IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE STREAM.** Clearing what a receiver has been shown and tearing down the agreement to send it more are two different acts; the second one is POST /admin-api/ssf/delete-stream. This receiver goes on taking delivery the moment this returns.

**AND IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE RECORD.** Every delivery wrote an `ssf.event.receive` row to the audit log, which has no clear operation anywhere — which is what makes it the durable half.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/signals` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body** (optional)

An empty object.

**200**: How many delivered events were dropped.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dropped` | integer |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

## GET /admin-api/ssf

`getSsf`

**The Shared Signals transmitter: its streams, their subjects, their queues and what a receiver refused**

Everything /admin/ssf draws, as JSON. Per stream: the configuration a receiver agreed, who it is about, what is waiting to be delivered, the counters, and the stream's own log — which is the only place a REFUSED PUSH is recorded, because a push a receiver rejected is invisible from the receiving end by definition.

SSF IS THE PIPE AND NOT THE VOCABULARY. It defines how two parties agree a stream, who the events are about (RFC 9493), what they travel in (RFC 8417) and how they get there (RFC 8935 push, RFC 8936 poll) — and two events of its own, both about the pipe. CAEP and RISC are the vocabularies spoken over it; CAEP is implemented and its own register is at GET /admin-api/caep, and RISC has one of its own at GET /admin-api/risc.

THE RECEIVER'S `authorization_header` IS NOT IN THIS REPLY. It is a credential belonging to somebody else's endpoint and it goes back only to the receiver that set it, at GET /ssf/stream.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ssf` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stream` | query | string |  | Only this stream. An exact stream id; applied before the streams are paged. |
| `streamsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the streams. Clamped, like every page parameter here. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |

**200**: The transmitter, its streams and what it has received.

## POST /admin-api/ssf/clear-dead-letters

`clearSsfDeadLetters`

**Drop a stream's dead letters**

Empties the stream's dead-letter queue: SETs that could not be delivered, each kept with its reason for `ssf.deadLetterRetentionS`. Nothing is sent. GET /admin-api/ssf lists them per stream as `deadLetters`.

## GET /admin-api/ssf/dead-letters

`getSsfDeadLetters`

**What the Shared Signals transmitter could not deliver, counted**

Everything /admin/ssf/dead-letters draws, as JSON: every Security Event Token held on a dead-letter queue in this realm, counted by cause, error code, the receiver's HTTP status and event type, over time across the retention window, and per stream with each push stream's delivery state — then the letters themselves, newest first, searched and paged, without their tokens.

**THE COUNTS ARE THE WHOLE REALM'S WHATEVER IS NARROWED.** `dlq`, `dlstream` and `dlcause` narrow `letters` and `matched` only.

**`process` IS THE ANSWERING PROCESS'S.** Its push cap is shared by every realm in that process, and its sweeps are its own; the rest is the shared store.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ssf/dead-letters` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dlq` | query | string |  | Narrows the letters to those whose jti, stream, reason, error code, status, event name, type URI or subject contains this. |
| `dlstream` | query | string |  | Only this stream's letters. An exact stream id. |
| `dlcause` | query | one of `push-failed`, `backlog-full`, `declared-dead`, `dead-stream` |  | Only letters of this cause. |
| `lettersPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the matched letters. Clamped, like every page parameter here. |
| `streamsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the streams holding a letter or not delivering, after `dlstream` and `dlcause` have narrowed them. It shares `per` with the letters. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |

**200**: The dead-letter queues of this realm, counted, and a page of their letters.

## POST /admin-api/ssf/delete

`deleteSsfStream`

**Delete a stream**

The stream, its subjects and everything queued on it. The receiver is NOT told — SSF has no event for "your stream is gone", and a stream-updated with status disabled would be a lie about something that still exists. A receiver finds out on its next call, with a 404 naming the stream_id.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/ssf` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/ssf/revive

`reviveSsfStream`

**Revive a dead push stream**

A push stream whose pushes have all failed for `ssf.deadStreamTimeoutS` is declared DEAD: nothing more is pushed to it, its SETs go to its dead-letter queue, and a sweep pushes one as a probe every period. This revives it at once, so the next SET is pushed. Refused for a stream that is not dead. The dead letters are kept, and nothing resends them.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/ssf` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string |  | Optional; written on the stream's log. |
| `stream_id` | string | yes | The stream. |

**200**: Confirmation, or a refusal naming the stream_id or saying it is not dead.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

## POST /admin-api/ssf/status

`setSsfStreamStatus`

**Enable, pause or disable a stream**

The three values and what separates them: a PAUSED stream keeps QUEUEING and delivers nothing, so what happened while it was paused is still there when it is enabled again; a DISABLED one DROPS what is waiting. That is the difference between "I was not listening" and "it did not happen", and it is the whole reason a Shared Signals receiver has a pause. A paused PUSH stream holds its SETs and pushes them, in order, when it is enabled again.

A change here also emits a **stream-updated** event ON the stream whether or not the receiver agreed that type (SSF 1.0 section 8.1.5), in the order that section requires: BEFORE the stream stops when it is paused or disabled, and after it starts again when it is enabled. Setting the status a stream already has announces nothing.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/ssf` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string |  | Optional. Why, in words — it rides in the stream-updated event's `reason` member, which nothing parses. |
| `status` | one of `enabled`, `paused`, `disabled` | yes | The new status. |
| `stream_id` | string | yes | The stream, as GET /admin-api/ssf lists it. |

**200**: What happened, and whether the stream-updated event went with it.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `report` | object |  |  |
| `report.claims` | any JSON |  | A Security Event Token's claims. An event's members are each event type's, and the claims are what was signed, so a model of them here would be a second list of every event type. A Security Event Token's claims. An event's members are each event type's, and the claims are what was signed, so a model of them here would be a second list of every event type. |
| `report.deadLettered` | boolean |  |  |
| `report.delivered` | boolean |  |  |
| `report.err` | string, or null |  |  |
| `report.held` | boolean |  |  |
| `report.jti` | string |  |  |

## POST /admin-api/ssf/transmit

`transmitSsfEvent`

**Send a Security Event Token on a stream**

Builds the SET, signs it with `ssf.signingAlgorithm`, queues it on the stream and — for a PUSH stream — POSTs it to the receiver's delivery endpoint. On a POLL stream it stays queued until the receiver asks.

**IT IS THE ONLY WAY AN EVENT HAPPENS HERE.** Nothing in this service watches a session and emits when it changes: SSF defines no event about a session, so a transmitter that invented one would be inventing a vocabulary. That changes with CAEP.

A failed push is NOT retried and the event stays on the queue. A service that retried would make a receiver's one-shot failure invisible — a client answering 500 then 202 looks, from its own logs, like a client that works.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/ssf` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `payload` | object |  | The event's own members. A verification event takes an optional `state`; a stream-updated event takes a required `status` and an optional `reason`. An unrecognised member is CARRIED with a warning rather than refused: an event vocabulary extends, and a receiver is expected to ignore what it does not know. |
| `stream_id` | string | yes | The stream. |
| `subject` | object |  | Optional `sub_id` (RFC 9493), simple or complex. Neither SSF event takes one — both are about the STREAM — so this is here for the vocabularies that come next. Each format's member set is CLOSED and an extra member is refused by name. |
| `txn` | string |  | Optional RFC 8417 `txn`, tying several events to one act. |
| `type` | string | yes | The event type URI. It must be one the stream DELIVERS — the intersection of what the receiver requested and what this transmitter supports — and a refusal lists what that is. |

**200**: The jti, whether it was delivered or only queued, and what the receiver said.

## GET /admin-api/ssf/transmitters

`getPartnerSignals`

**The federation partners whose Shared Signals this realm receives**

Everything /admin/ssf/transmitters draws: each federation relationship whose signals are on (its kind — `sign-in` or `signals-only` — SSF issuer, discovered configuration, delivery, stream, counts and blocks), every Security Event Token that arrived with whether it verified, the person it named and what it led to, the sign-ins partners have blocked and the account locks a signals-only partner put on people here. Never a secret. `relationship` narrows what arrived. What arrived, the blocks and the locks are each one page, moved by `receivedPage`, `blocksPage` and `locksPage` with `per` shared, and described by `paging`. A partner's stream is configured on its relationship and acted on with `POST /admin-api/federation/signals-*`.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/ssf/transmitters` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `relationship` | query | string |  | Only what arrived from this relationship. Applied before what arrived is paged. |
| `receivedPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of what arrived, newest first. Clamped, like every page parameter here. |
| `blocksPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the sign-ins partners blocked. |
| `locksPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the account locks partners put on people here. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page, shared by the three lists. |

## POST /admin-api/ssf/verify

`verifySsfStream`

**Send a transmitter-initiated verification event**

SSF 1.0 section 8.1.4: a transmitter MAY send a verification event at any time. This sends one on the stream with NO `state` — section 8.1.4.2 forbids a state the receiver did not supply — whether or not the stream agreed the type. A paused push stream holds it until it is enabled; a disabled stream refuses it. `ssf.verificationEveryS` does the same on a schedule.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/ssf` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream_id` | string | yes | The stream. |
